The petitioner has filed the petition under Section 22 of the Employment Compensation Act, 1923 for claiming compensation for the injured sustained in the incident occurred on 06.11.2015 arising out of and during the course of doing his duty under the employment of the Respondent No.1.

The Petitioner was sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident dated 06.11.2015, hence petitioner has filed present claim petition claiming compensation and accordingly as per Judgment dated 20.11.2017 this Court has dismissed the claim petition on the ground that the relationship of employer and employee has not been established.

Thereafter the Petitioner being aggrieved by the judgment and award dated 20.11.2017 has filed appeal in MFA No.9064/2018 before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and that matter was disposed on dated 12.11.2024 by setting aside the judgment and award dated 20.11.2017 with respect to present matter and remanded back to this court for fresh consideration to enable the Claimant to adduce further evidence to establish his case and accordingly present matter is restore to its file to decided the matter afresh, provided reasonable opportunity to both parties to adduced further evidence.

Admittedly, the respondents No.1 and 2 are the brothers and they constitutes HUF and they are joint and they have not partitioned their family properties and they have purchased the offending vehicle in favour of respondent No.1 and the Respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle and he has employed the petitioner as driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, petitioner has sustained injuries due to alleged incident during the course of employment under the respondent No.1.

As such there is no employer and employee relationship between the petitioner and Respondent No.1 and therefore Respondent No.3/Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation and prayed to dismiss the claim ECA.75/2016 18 SCCH - 7 petition against the Respondent No.3.

On going through the prosecution papers, complaint, mahazar, Inquest mahazar,
Postmortem report, Charge Sheet, pleadings and materials available on record and the evidence of PW-1 are specific to the effect that, the respondent No.1 is the RC owner of the of offending vehicle in question and the petitioner was under employment of the Respondent No.1 at the time of the alleged accident and he was giving Rs.10,000/-per month and daily bata of Rs.100/- and during the course of the employment/doing driving work under the employment of the Respondent No.1 the alleged accident occurred.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged ECA.75/2016 19 SCCH - 7 by the prosecution, at the time of alleged accident, when the Petitioner/accused drove the offending Maruthi Ertiga Car bearing Reg. No.KA-02-MJ-2783 along with Respondent No.2 and Ramesh as inmates and he drove the same in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endangering human life, at that time suddenly a horse entered into the road and therefore in order to avoid dashing, he drove towards left side and dashed against the divider, as a result the Petitioner/accused has sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, R.W.2, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P.2/Complaint,
Ex.P.3/ Charge Sheet, Ex.P.7/Spot Sketch, Ex.P.4/Spot Mahazar and Ex.P.8/Wound Certificate clearly establishes that the alleged incident occurred at the spot.
It is not in dispute as to the aspect that, the injured Petitioner sustained grievous injuries during the course of the employment and sustained injuries in the alleged accident.

Because, for the above reasons collectively, it is clear that,
the incident happened due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by the Petitioner and due to such negligent act the Petitioner himself has sustained injuries in the alleged accident.
It is evident that injuries and cause of injuries to Petitioner noted in the Ex.P8/Wound Certificate would be caused by the alleged ECA.75/2016 20 SCCH - 7 incident as a result of RTA.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged incident was occurred due involvement of the offending vehicle.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC.
Thus because of such accident, it resulted in the injury of the Petitioner aforesaid.
Therefore, the alleged incident occurred due to the fault and negligence of the Petitioner/accused.
In view of the above discussion this court is of the view that the Respondent No.1 is the employer and he has appointed the injured Petitioner as driver to drive the offending vehicle.

This court is on the further view that in the absence of the written contract between the Petitioner and Respondent No.1, in view of the admission of employment of Petitioner under Respondent No.1 in his written statement, it is admitted fact that the Respondent No.1 is the employer and the Petitioner is an employee and the same is established by the material available on record and evidence of PW-1 and R.W.2.

Hence I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved there was an employer and employee relationship in between the Petitioner and respondent No.1 and during the course of employment this incident was took place ECA.75/2016 21 SCCH - 7 and the Petitioner has sustained injuries due to the alleged accident.
Hence, I answered the Issue No.1 and 2 in the affirmative.

Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition.
With regard to the income of the deceased the petitioner has not produced any acceptable evidence.
Hence, in the absence of material evidence with regard to the monthly income of the deceased, by considering nature of work of deceased, the notional income of the deceased is considered.

The Government of India, through notification S.O. 71(E) dated January 3, 2020, has enhanced the wage ceiling under the Employee's Compensation Act, 1923, from Rs. 8,000/- to Rs.
15,000/- per month, with effect from the date of publication of the notification in the Official Gazette.
This revision is in exercise of the powers conferred under sub-section (1B) of Section 4 of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923.

The notification supersedes the previous notification S.O.
1258(E), dated May 31st, 2010, which had earlier set the wage ceiling at Rs. 8,000/- per month.

Accordingly income of the deceased is considered at Rs.8,000/- p.m.

27. The income of the petitioner is considered at Rs. 8,000/-
p.m. and further as per Section 4 of Employee's Compensation Act, 1923 the petitioner is entitled to compensation an amount equal to 60% of the monthly wages of the injured multiplied by relevant factor or amount of Rs.1,40,000/- whichever is more.
In this present case on hand the income of the petitioner is considered at Rs.8,000/- p.m.
Hence 60% of the monthly wages comes to Rs.4,800/-.
Further as on the ECA.75/2016 25 SCCH - 7 date of the accident the petitioner was aged about 52 years.
As per schedule IV the relevant factor for 52 years is 146.20.

The 60% of the monthly wages comes to Rs.4,800/- and it is to be multiplied by the relevant factor i.e., Rs.4,800/- X 146.20 =
Rs.7,01,760/-.
As held above the petitioner is having permanent disability at 20%.

As per Section 4(c) of Employee's Compensation Act,1923 where permissible partial disablement result from the injury (i) in the case of an injury specified in Part II of Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation which would have been payable in the case of permanent total disablement is specified therein as being the percentage of the loss of earning capacity caused by the injury, (ii) in case of an injury not specified in Schedule I, such percentage of the compensation payable in the case of permanent total disablement as is proportionate to the loss of earning capacity permanently caused by the petitioner.

In this case on hand based on the evidence of PW.2 the functional disabilities is considered at 20% and out of Rs.7,01,760/-, 20% comes to Rs.1,40,352/-
(Rs.7,01,760/- X 20/100).
Hence the petitioner entitled for compensation of Rs.1,40,352/- under the head of loss of income.
. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.12 for an amount of Rs.1,36,412/- and Ex.P.20 for an amount of Rs.3,24,146/-.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,60,558/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses.

Hence the petitioner is entitled for just and reasonable compensation amount of Rs.6,00,910/-.
